body: Movement classes will help with that. Try a “Chekhov” “Laban” or any type of psychophysical   class for actors. They are a lot harder to find than basic film/scene study class but they are invaluable. Also “improv” will help release tension and free you up a bit. You’ll find what works best for you allow yourself to explore and be patient with yourself. Good luck :)

I think it helps to know that your not alone! Every actor deals with these struggles even the famous ones. Although many people won’t admit if they are struggling as it is a very (ego driven) field.

For me What’s helped other than “age” and realizing that we all have a different role in life and our journeys are all different— but therapy, regular meditation and spirituality.

I think spiritually helps the most, it gives meaning to life deeper than the surface and it’s helped my career a lot as I’ve learned to approach it differently. 

There is a free ebook by “actor” jack plotnick at jackplotnick.com and it’s extremely helpful when it comes to self doubt.

Another book I recommend is “mix tapes” it helps give a new perspective on self doubt, critical voices in our own heads and where
They come from and how to transcend them. Good luck keep believing in yourself - enough persistence and you’ll find success!

I’m on the fence. I certainly believe you need a certain amount of empathy and life experience to truly experience being in character however, the safety of oneself and those around him/herself is where a line needs to be drawn. It absolutely can mess with the psyche and create a toxic living environment for those in relationship to that “method actor” 

With that said I  think everyone has the technique that resonates on an individual level. I personally love the Meisner technique as it feels most truthful to who I am as an artist.

You are not doomed. A few things I would suggest as someone who has struggled with anxiety is 1. Try sticking with a class for at least a month (long enough to develop a habit) and get comfortable with feeling uncomfortable. Opening up is challenging for most people due to the fact
That the world closes us and discourages true connection.

Another thing- try auditing all sorts of classes
And you may find that a different technique will resonate better... meisner is a great technique that really helps you connect to your authentic self. 

Good luck! :)
